function: QRMP-DQN agents learn STAR-RIS element mode and phase shifts plus users' channel assignment, power allocation and task splitting ratio; computing resources by convex KKT (pp. 8-10).
system: Narrow-band uplink SGF-NOMA, single-antenna BS with MEC server, 3 static and 6-10 mobile users, mode-switching STAR-RIS with 30 elements (20-60 varied), 1 GHz carrier (pp. 4-6, 11-12, 14).
method: QRMP-DQN: multi-agent parameterized-action DQN with quantile regression and a deterministic actor; reinforcement learning, centralized training, decentralized execution, hidden layers 256 and 128 (pp. 8-11).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rayleigh BS-user fading, Rician STAR-RIS links with array response, path-loss exponents 2.2, 2.8, 3.6, directional-walk mobility, statistical CSI error; no dataset or measurements (pp. 5, 11).
test_conditions: Simulated 3D environment; each point averages 200 episodes after sufficient training, with MUs (6-10), channels, STAR-RIS elements (20-60), power or delay limit varied; no unseen-condition test stated (pp. 11-14).
baselines: Learned: conventional MP-DQN, DQN+DDPG, reflecting-only RIS with DDPG. Non-learned: random STAR-RIS coefficients, fixed task splitting ratio, fixed power. Variants: OMA, no RIS (pp. 11-14).
metrics: Average energy consumption (J) of mobile users, average data rate, convergence versus episodes (pp. 12-14).
complexity: Training O(E*T*B*n*((|s_n|+K*N_d)(G+2)+K*N_d*|s_n|)) and testing forward pass O((2(|s_n|+G+3)+K*N_d)*n); no runtime (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 5: "we apply the Rayleigh fading model as the small-scale fading for BS-user links and the Rician fading model for BS-STAR-RIS and STAR-RIS-user links"; custom simulator with textbook fading, no 3GPP model, public ray-tracing set or measured data.
q2_support: p. 12: "each point in the figures below is obtained by averaging the results of 200 episodes after sufficient training"; the sweeps over MUs, channels, STAR-RIS elements, power and CSI error are reported per setting, and no passage tests a trained policy in an unseen setting or adapts it.
q3_support: p. 11: "we utilize benchmark cases of Conventional MP-DQN, DQN [45]+DDPG, Random TARCs and Fixed task splitting ratio (TSR)"; on average energy consumption the proposed method beats MP-DQN and DQN+DDPG (Fig. 5, p. 12) and random STAR-RIS coefficients (Fig. 7, p. 12).
q4_support: p. 11: "In the testing stage, the complexity is only determined by the forward propagation of QRMP-DQN agents"; the same subsection gives O(.) expressions for training and for testing.
q5_support: p. 11: "We list the detailed simulation parameters in Table II unless otherwise specified"; the channels come from a custom simulator, and the paper gives no link or DOI for code or data.
notes: Area 3: the STAR-RIS element agents learn the mode and phase shifts (p. 9), a physical-layer decision learned jointly with task splitting and channel assignment, so the work passes above_phy; computing resources are not learned (convex KKT, p. 10). q1: Rayleigh and Rician fading only. q2: no unseen-condition test; the MU-agent state holds the channel gains of all MUs and channels (p. 7), so each sweep point probably needs its own training, but the paper does not say. q3: MP-DQN is the base of QRMP-DQN and may be read as an ablation, but DQN+DDPG, DDPG for the reflecting-only RIS, random STAR-RIS coefficients and the fixed task splitting ratio meet the rule. OMA and no-RIS curves are protocol or system variants, not baselines.
